title: From Minimum Wage America to Australian Pay: Your Hourly to Annual Guide with Casual Loading and Super
description: Compare minimum wage america with Australian rates. Learn how casual loading and super affect your annual pay. Use our hourly to annual calculator for 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week, with casual loading adding 25% to reach $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How is annual pay calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Annual gross pay is calculated by multiplying your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. So annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives a base figure before tax, super, and any loadings.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply on top of super?
faqs.a: Yes. Casual loading (typically 25%) is paid on top of your base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. Superannuation is then calculated at 12% of your ordinary earnings, which includes the casual loading. Super is paid on top of your gross pay, not deducted from it.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries or occupations by the Fair Work Commission. Many workers are entitled to award rates, which vary by role and experience. The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you're comparing job offers or planning your budget, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a straightforward calculation. But in Australia, the picture includes casual loading, superannuation, and tax – and it's different from what you might see in discussions about **minimum wage america**. This guide walks you through the key numbers and assumptions.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week – the ordinary hours under many awards and the National Employment Standards. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust accordingly. For example, a part-time worker on 20 hours per week would use 20 in the formula.

Using the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026):
- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1004.72 (rounded to $1004.90 in official figures)
- Fortnightly: $1004.72 × 2 = $2009.44
- Annual: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44

This is your gross pay before any loadings, super, or tax. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base rate and see these figures instantly.

### Casual Loading: What It Means

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a loading – usually 25% – on top of your base rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. The Fair Work Ombudsman sets this loading in many awards.

For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). That changes the annual calculation:
- Weekly: $33.05 × 38 = $1255.90
- Fortnightly: $1255.90 × 2 = $2511.80
- Annual: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80

Note: When using our calculator, enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading). Then check the box to add 25% casual loading. Never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

For more detail, see our page on [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings (including casual loading if applicable) and is paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It does not reduce your take-home pay. The maximum contribution base for super is $270,830 per year (2026–27), so super stops accruing once your earnings exceed that threshold.

Using the casual example above:
- Annual ordinary earnings: $65,306.80
- Super contribution: 12% × $65,306.80 = $7,836.82
- Total cost to employer: $65,306.80 + $7,836.82 = $73,143.62

Your pay slip will show your gross pay and the super contribution separately.

### Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy (generally 2%). The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Above that, rates are:
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare is calculated on your taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners (using 2025–26 single thresholds as 2026–27 reductions were not confirmed).

For a casual worker earning $65,306.80 annually, the estimated tax (excluding Medicare) would be:
- First $18,200: $0
- Next $26,800 (to $45,000): 15% = $4,020
- Remaining $20,306.80 (to $65,306.80): 30% = $6,092.04
- Total tax: $10,112.04
- Plus Medicare 2% on $65,306.80 = $1,306.14
- Total deductions: $11,418.18
- Estimated take-home: $53,888.62

This is an estimate only. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for more detail.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. Knowing your fortnightly gross helps with budgeting. For the casual rate above, fortnightly gross is $2,511.80. After tax and Medicare (roughly $439 per fortnight), you'd take home about $2,073 per fortnight.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Average Earnings

The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour) is the legal floor. But most employees are covered by awards that set higher minimums. For example, the General Retail Industry Award has different rates for different classifications. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award.

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. That's about $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week – well above the minimum. All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These are averages across all industries and states, not medians for a specific job.

### How This Compares to Minimum Wage America

Discussions about **minimum wage america** often focus on the federal rate of US$7.25 per hour (as of 2026), though many states set higher minimums. Converting to Australian dollars (say AUD 1.50 per USD) gives about AUD $10.88 per hour – far below Australia's minimum. But direct comparisons are tricky because of different social safety nets, healthcare, and superannuation. In Australia, the casual loading and super guarantee add significant value on top of the hourly rate.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more reference tables and data, visit our [reference tables](/data) page. You can also learn about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) to optimise your total compensation.
